judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under Grade R (rank 0) Emergent Writing, and both concern copying print (shared LC tag 'copying'/'copying print', shared token 'copies'). The second SFI is anchored to Term 2, Sub-strand 'Emergent Writing': incidental, play-based, spontaneous copying of environmental print such as product labels. The first SFI is anchored to Term 4, Sub-strand 'Emergent Handwriting': deliberate copying of defined units (patterns, words and letters) as directed handwriting practice. Within Grade R this is an earlier-Term to later-Term direction (Term 2 -> Term 4), permitted, and the change is substantive rather than repeated wording: incidental play copying of print develops the print-awareness and visual-motor copying behaviour that supports later intentional, accurate copying of patterns, words and letters. Direction is therefore second_to_first. Confidence is moderated because the two statements sit in different sub-strands (emergent writing awareness vs handwriting motor control) and source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), so the dependency is inferred coherence rather than an explicit CAPS sequencing statement.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills resolve to the same coordinate (Grade 2, rank 2) and the same Term 4 / Reading and Phonics / Group Guided Reading scope, taken from rows 5 and 4 of the same source table cell. 'Uses self-correcting strategies when reading: re-reading, pausing, practising a word before saying it aloud' and 'Reads with increasing fluency and speed using correct pronunciation' are complementary oral-reading expectations within the same guided-reading programme: monitoring/repair routines and the accuracy-plus-smoothness target reinforce each other instructionally. This is more than shared wording or shared ancestry (which alone would not suffice): the pair-specific coherence is that both govern how a Grade 2 learner handles words aloud during guided reading. However, the bounded evidence shows no substantive extension, broadening, or increase in complexity of one over the other; they are simultaneous, co-listed Term 4 expectations at the identical rank, so a same-rank buildsTowards claim is not substantiated and no developmental direction is asserted. Judged relatesTo, symmetric, with canonical endpoint order preserved. Confidence is moderate because both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted excerpts each), the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs are distinct printed bullets in the same Grade 3, Term 1, WRITING table under the sub-strand 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' (same coordinate rank 3, same term, same page 113). 'Talks to a partner to begin planning writing' is an oral pre-writing/planning behaviour (LC tags: oral, partner talk, planning, writing), while 'Uses phonic knowledge and spelling rules to write unfamiliar words' is a transcription/encoding skill (LC tags: phonics, spelling, unfamiliar words, writing). They are complementary components of the same writing process rather than one supporting success in the other: partner planning talk does not enable phonic spelling, and spelling knowledge does not enable collaborative planning. Shared parentage and the single shared token 'writing' alone would not establish a relation, but the two bullets are co-taught elements of one writing task within the same sub-strand, giving substantive instructional coherence without dependency or sequence; same-Term placement also provides no developmental ordering evidence. Evidence limitation: source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so unseen qualifiers could not be inspected.

judgment.rationale: Both SFIs sit under GRADE 1 HOME LANGUAGE ENGLISH (resolved coordinate Grade 1, rank 1), but in different terms and skill areas: the second is Grade 1 / Term 1 / Reading and Phonics / Phonics ('Recognises and names some letters of the alphabet: 2 vowels and at least 6 consonants', LCs tagged alphabet/letters/phonics/recognises/names), while the first is Grade 1 / Term 2 / Writing / Handwriting ('Forms some frequently used capital letters correctly (e.g. A, C, H, I, T, W)', LC tagged capital letters/handwriting/letter formation). Alphabetic knowledge - identifying and naming individual letters - plausibly supports success in correctly forming named letters in handwriting, so the direction runs from the Term 1 recognition/naming skill to the Term 2 formation skill, which is also the only permitted within-grade order (earlier Term to later Term). The shared lexical token 'letters' alone would not suffice; the judgment rests on the substantive letter-knowledge-to-letter-formation link. Confidence is moderate because the two statements lie in different skill areas (recognition versus motor production) and the source evidence excerpts for both endpoints are truncated.

judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 3 Reading and Phonics Skills under the 'Phonic Activities' sub-strand. The second SFI (identity scope grade=grade 3|term=term 1) is the revision/consolidation of vowel digraphs already taught in Grade 2 ('oo', 'ee', 'ea', 'ai', 'oa', 'ay'); the first SFI (grade=grade 3|term=term 4) extends vowel recognition to more complex r-controlled/split patterns (-ere in 'here', -air in 'hair', -are in 'square'), consistent with the Term 4 row context 'Revise the phonics taught so far and introduce more complex combinations'. Secure recognition of the simpler Grade 2 vowel digraphs in Term 1 supports success with the more complex Term 4 vowel patterns, so the permitted direction is earlier Term 1 (second) to later Term 4 (first) within the same grade. Shared tag 'phonics' and wording overlap alone were not treated as sufficient; the pair-specific increase in phonic complexity is the basis. Both endpoints carry truncated source evidence and upstream merge/audit context, so judgement rests on the full statement text and resolved Grade/Term identity scopes available.

Secure Grade 2 self-monitoring of word recognition and meaning therefore supports success with the Grade 3 expectation, rather than being mere wording repetition. However, the second statement's demands (attentive listening to a read-aloud, then drawing and captioning) are not a deepening or extension of picture-based prediction in emergent reading; proficiency in predicting from pictures does not specifically underwrite listening enjoyment or caption writing, so no developmental dependency is evidenced despite the admissible Term 1 to Term 3 forward direction. Shared ancestor is only the Grade 1 banner and the lexical overlap is limited to 'picture'/'story', which alone is not progression evidence. Secure letter-sound/digraph recognition is precisely the phonic knowledge drawn on when spelling words correctly, so proficiency in the first supports success in the second; the reverse is less supported because correct spelling presupposes rather than establishes digraph recognition. Same-grade/same-term direction is permitted (earlier-or-same term) and rests on the substantive specific-to-generalised-application shift, not repeated wording. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts supplied.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Grade R (rank 0) Skills. Second: Term 3, Emergent Writing / Works with words — "Uses terms like 'beginning', 'middle', 'end', 'sound', 'word', 'letter' when talking about texts". These are complementary emergent-literacy capabilities that cohere substantively: shared whole-class engagement with enlarged texts and the use of print/text metalanguage when talking about texts reinforce one another within Grade R. However, they are distinct capabilities located in different Skill Areas and Sub-strands, and the supplied evidence shows no substantive extension, deepening or increased complexity of one capability into the other, so a developmental buildsTowards claim is not supported; the coherence is more than shared wording or the common Grade R ancestor, so no_relation would understate it. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the correct judgment. They are substantively coherent complementary writing skills — accurate print-script letter formation and frame-supported independent composition are two facets of the same term's writing programme, and their Learning Components tag handwriting/print script versus story/paragraph/writing frame, so this is not mere repeated wording (single shared token 'writes', jaccard 0.04) or generic recurrence. But the evidence places them as concurrent Grade 2 Term 2 requirements with no substantive extension, broadening, or increased complexity of one into the other, so a same-rank, same-term buildsTowards is not warranted on this bounded evidence; a general transcription-supports-composition argument is not pair-specific curricular evidence of developmental dependency. Canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the supported judgment. Shared ancestry, page proximity (page 94) and local rank proximity were treated as nomination signals only, not as semantic support. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

The shared parent, same term, same page and token overlap ('a', 'and', 'to', 'uses') are weak signals only and do not establish developmental direction, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit under the identical Grade 1 / Term 2 / Writing / 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' path (same canonical rank 1, same term), so direction cannot rest on coordinate order and needs substantive content evidence. The second SFI ('Draws pictures to convey a message, adding a label or caption... about a personal experience', LCs: draws pictures to convey a message; adds a label or caption to a drawing) is word/phrase-level emergent composing anchored in drawing, and its LC claims recur in earlier-grade/term contexts, marking it as the less complex writing unit. The first SFI ('Writes sentences using words containing the phonic sounds already taught', LC tags: phonics, sentences, spelling, writing) requires sustained sentence-level construction with applied phonic/spelling knowledge. Proficiency in captioning and labelling one's own drawing with a message plausibly supports success at writing full sentences from taught phonic sounds, so a same-term buildsTowards from the second to the first is semantically supported rather than mere shared-parent or shared 'writing' LC-token overlap (jaccard 0.09) or page proximity. Confidence is moderated because both appear as co-taught Term 2 bullets and endpoint source/LC evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each), so the ordering is inferred from statement complexity rather than explicit sequencing text.

Shared tokens are limited to 'common' and the tag 'phonics', so the relation rests on substantive complementary content, not wording or shared hierarchy. Canonical relatesTo (null direction) is therefore the complete judgment.
